title: Industry Structure

learningObjectives.text: Know and understand the following concepts: C4 ratio, HHI
learningObjectives.src: course-data.js Session 3 'Read: Chapter 7'; S03 slides p.3

learningObjectives.text: Know how to calculate various measures of industry concentration and how they relate to market competitiveness
Understand the limitations of concentration measures

keyTerms.def: An industry is 'concentrated' when a few large firms control the industry (e.g., Auto, Airline, etc.).
Industry concentration and market competitiveness are inversely related (i.e., monopoly at 100% vs. perfect competition at ≈ 0%).
The fraction of total sales generated by the four largest firms in the industry (ranges from 0 = extremely competitive to 1 = highly concentrated).
The sum of the squared market shares of firms in a given industry multiplied by 10,000 (ranges from 0 = extremely competitive to 10,000 = monopoly).

vars.w_i: market share of firm i as a decimal

workedExamples.name: US mobile telecom 2013
workedExamples.givens: Verizon 42%, AT&T 33%, Sprint 16%, T-Mobile 3%; remaining 6% treated as one firm

workedExamples.name: Allegiant airports (Dec 2025 BTS data)
workedExamples.givens: OAK vs SFO, HOU vs IAH, MDW vs ORD shares
workedExamples.answer: OAK HHI 7,323 C4 95.4% vs SFO 2,765 / 76.8%; HOU 8,939 / 98.8% vs IAH 3,602 / 78.7%; MDW 8,632 / 99.2% vs ORD 2,503 / 78.2%. Allegiant cities are more concentrated, consistent with its strategy of avoiding competition at smaller airports.

cases: US domestic airlines 2025: C4 = 64.4%, HHI = 1,162 (S03 slides p.12)
Route-level HHIs 2025: National 1,162; LAS-LAX 1,620; ATL-MCO 5,324; LAX-SFO 2,104; ORD-LGA 3,227; LAX-JFK 3,433 (S03 slides p.14)
US autos 2025 all firms: GM 18, Toyota 16, Ford 14, Hyundai/Kia 11; C4 59%, HHI 2,578. Domestic only: GM 50, Ford 39, Tesla 10, Rivian 1; C4 100%, HHI 4,122 (S03 slides p.15)
Change in avg top-4 share by sector 1997-2017: increasing lack of competition (S03 slides p.10)
Allegiant business model: low-cost, leisure-only, ~75% of routes no nonstop competition, ancillary $76.35/passenger in 2025 (S03 workbook Solution!B18)
usefulness: Useful in quantifying industry rivalry, degree of buyer, and supplier power (S03 p.10)
Used by the Justice Department when determining whether to approve a merger (S03 p.10)
C4 and HHI positively correlated; C4 uses top four firms, HHI uses all firms; HHI squares shares so it places greater weight on firms with larger shares (S03 p.11)
limitations: Do the relevant companies compete at a national, regional, or local level? (S03 p.17)
Do the measures account for foreign imports? (S03 p.17)
In what product segments do firms actually compete? (S03 p.17)
traps: Use shares as decimals before squaring (42% → 0.42), then ×10,000
Treat 'remaining share' as one firm only when told (professor's telecom convention)
C4 can be identical while HHI differs (telecom 2013 vs 2014: both 94%, HHI 3,154 vs 2,706)
spreadsheetTasks: S03 In-Class Exercise: compute C4 and HHI for 3 Allegiant airports vs comparison airports; judge strategic fit
